prompt:
Solve the running-time recurrence below.

```formula
T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n^2
where
T: the running time on input size n
n: the input size
In words: Two half-size calls are followed by quadratic outside work.
```

options.explanation:
Correct. The critical exponent is one; quadratic outside work is larger by a full power, and children together cost half the parent’s outside work.

```formula
log_2(2) = 1
f(n) = n^2
2(n/2)^2 = n^2/2
where
f: the work outside the recursive calls
log_2: the base-2 logarithm; log_2(x) is the power you raise 2 to in order to get x
n: the input size
In words: The critical exponent is one; quadratic outside work is larger by a full power, and children together cost half the parent’s outside work.
```

This incorrectly keeps quadratic work unchanged on every level. The actual level totals halve.

workedExample:
Identify the recursive parameters, then check root domination and regularity:

```formula
a = 2,  b = 2,  f(n) = n^2
c = log_2(2) = 1
f(n) = n^2 = Ω(n^{1 + ε}),  ε = 1
af(n / b) = 2 × (n / 2)^2 = n^2 / 2
n^2 / 2 ≤ qf(n),  q = 1/2 < 1
T(n) = Θ(f(n)) = Θ(n^2)
where
T(n): the running time on input size n
log_2: the base-2 logarithm; log_2(x) is the power you raise 2 to in order to get x
a: the number of recursive calls per call
b: the shrink factor
f(n): the work outside the recursive calls
n: the input size
c: the critical exponent log_b(a)
ε: epsilon, the margin by which f is polynomially larger (here 1)
q: the regularity constant, which must be below 1
Ω: Big-Omega, at least a constant times
Θ: Big-Theta, exactly this rate up to constants
≤: less than or equal to
In words: the root's n^2 work beats the n leaves by a whole power of n, and the children together do only half the parent's work, so the root dominates.
```

Level work halves each time, so its geometric sum is below twice the root’s quadratic contribution. The root dominates.
